subject: Renewal negotiation – hybrid consumption floor & expansion accelerator
messages:
From: Aron Beck <aron.beck@novumsystems.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — pricing posture and headroom needs

Hi Markus / Marissa,

Thanks for the renewal reminder. We're entering a heavier Q3 roadmap and want two things from the next term: predictability for budget planning and room to scale quickly if our model usage spikes. Current thinking on our side: keep a modest committed floor to preserve discounting, but build an overlay that credits rapid growth in the first 60 days of any spike.

Concretely: can Redwood put together an option that reduces the hard commit in year 1 by ~30% vs today's level but layers an "expansion accelerator" giving us back credits (or retroactive rebates) for the first 1M tokens of growth each quarter? We'd also like an option where invoice timing shifts to monthly in arrears rather than upfront for the reserved piece.

Attached our Q1 usage snapshot so you can model. Happy to jump on a 30m call this week.

Thanks,
Aron
VP Product, Novum Systems
[Attachment: Novum_usage_Q1_2028.csv (text/csv)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Aron Beck <aron.beck@novumsystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing posture and headroom needs

Aron — appreciate the clear ask and the usage file. High level we can do two parallel options for the renewal:

1) Hybrid Floor: lower baseline commit in Y1 (–30% as you suggested) with a consumption floor that scales up on a quarterly cadence. This preserves a modest discounted rate on the floor.

2) Expansion Accelerator: for bursts above forecast, provide an on-ramp credit equal to 40% of the incremental token cost for the first 1M growth tokens per quarter (effectively a temporary rebate to soften spike economics). Credits apply as a rebate on the next invoice or can be booked as an offset if you prefer.

We can also flip invoice timing to monthly for the reserved component for an incremental fee (or offset via a reduced upfront discount).

I've looped in Marissa (pricing) and Kimberly (commercial ops) to sketch the numbers and David (finance) to sanity-check invoicing/recognition. I'm attaching a short proposal we can use as a starting point.

If that aligns I'll schedule a 30m to walk the options and get to a mutual action plan.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Novum_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Novum proposal draft — numbers and ramp scenarios

Team — draft pricing notes to bring to the customer call: 

- Option A (Lower Floor + Standard Discount): Year 1 floor at 70% of current commit; 8% discount on floor rate; overage at pay-as-you-go with standard rates.
- Option B (Lower Floor + Accelerator): Year 1 floor at 70%; same 8% floor discount; expansion accelerator = 40% credit on incremental cost for first 1M growth tokens per quarter; credit applied as invoice rebate.
- Invoice cadence: Upfront annual prepay (baseline) or monthly arrears for baseline with 1.5% uplift to effective price.
- Legal: draft SOW amendment to add the accelerator clause + credit mechanics; need to confirm tax/recognition with finance.

Attachments: updated proposal (see Markus). Please review the model assumptions in tab "Novum Model" on page 2 — I simulated three growth profiles (flat, seasonal spike, sustained growth).

Next actions: Kimberly to confirm credit accounting flow and whether credits can be auto-applied. David to confirm revenue recognition impact for monthly arrears. Markus to run the customer call and capture selection.

— Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Aron Beck <aron.beck@novumsystems.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing posture and headroom needs

Thanks Markus — the two-option approach looks sensible. A couple items from our side:

- We prefer Option B (Accelerator) but would like the first step of the floor to be at 60% (not 70%) and then step to 80% after quarter 2 contingent on usage. That gives us runway to prove the re-platform.
- Instead of a 1.5% uplift for monthly arrears, would you consider removing the uplift if we commit to a 6-month minimum pre-commit at the reduced floor? Essentially a hybrid invoice cadence: monthly, but with a rolling 6-month minimum guarantee.
- Can credits be issued as a true-time invoice credit (not later rebate)? It's important for our cash flow to see those credits on the next invoice.

I've inline-quoted your earlier email below for context. Happy to take the call Thursday 3/15 at 10am PT.

On Mon, Mar 12, 2028 at 11:05 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Aron — appreciate the clear ask and the usage file. High level we can do two parallel options for the renewal:
>

> 2) Expansion Accelerator: for bursts above forecast, provide an on-ramp credit equal to 40% of the incremental token cost for the first 1M growth tokens per quarter (effectively a temporary rebate to soften spike economics).
>

Regards,
Aron
VP Product, Novum Systems

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Aron Beck <aron.beck@novumsystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing posture and headroom needs

Aron — thanks, that feedback is helpful and doable. Agreed on a path forward:

- We'll prepare a formal amendment with Option B as primary and Option A as fallback. For Option B we'll model your requested floor step: 60% in Q1–Q2, automatic step to 80% starting Q3 if month-over-month usage stays within the agreed band.
- Credits from the Expansion Accelerator will be applied as invoice line-item credits on the immediate next invoice (not a delayed rebate). Kimberly to confirm mechanics; David to confirm accounting entry.
- For invoice cadence: we'll offer monthly arrears with a 6-month rolling minimum guarantee in place of a 1.5% uplift. If Novum elects to remove the minimum at any time, the uplift will apply.

Next steps: Kimberly will send the credit flow and accounting note by EOD Friday, Mar 16. Marissa and I will finalize the amendment and send a DocuSign link once legal signs off. We'll target an executed amendment by Mar 23 so the new term can start Apr 1.

I'll schedule the 3/15 10am PT call on your calendar and send an agenda (30m).

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
